Configure a 2D square cavity natural convection simulation corresponding to the de Vahl Davis benchmark case.
The cavity has side length L = 0.1 m and is filled with air.
Use OpenFOAM solver buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam to solve the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations coupled with the Boussinesq buoyancy approximation in transient mode.
Set gravity vector g = (0, -9.81, 0), acting in the negative y-direction.
The left wall (x = 0) is the hot wall with fixedValue temperature T = 300 K.
The right wall (x = 0.1 m) is the cold wall with fixedValue temperature T = 290 K.
The top wall and bottom wall are adiabatic; apply zeroGradient boundary condition for temperature on both.
Apply noSlip velocity boundary condition on all four walls.
Set reference temperature T_ref = 295 K for the Boussinesq linearization.
Use air properties evaluated at 295 K: thermal expansion coefficient beta = 1/295 K^-1, kinematic viscosity nu = 1.5e-5 m^2/s, thermal diffusivity alpha = 2.1e-5 m^2/s.
The resulting Rayleigh number is approximately 1.05e6, consistent with the standard de Vahl Davis Ra = 10^6 case.
Generate a uniform 200x200 structured mesh over the square domain [0, 0.1] x [0, 0.1] in the x and y directions respectively.
Initialize the velocity field to zero everywhere and initialize the temperature field to a linear profile from 300 K at x = 0 to 290 K at x = 0.1 m.
Set deltaT = 0.01 s, writeControl = timeStep, writeInterval = 100, endTime = 100 s.
Use pimple algorithm with nOuterCorrectors = 2, nCorrectors = 2, nNonOrthogonalCorrectors = 1.
Solve pressure with GAMG solver and tolerance 1e-7, solve velocity with smoothSolver (Gauss-Seidel) with tolerance 1e-6, solve temperature with smoothSolver (Gauss-Seidel) with tolerance 1e-6.
Use corrected schemes for ddt, grad, div, and laplacian terms in fvSchemes to ensure second-order accuracy.
Set initial pressure p_rgh boundary conditions as zeroGradient on all walls.
Set initial velocity boundary conditions as fixedValue (0,0,0) on all walls.
